resources.title: Molecular, Cellular, and Tissue Biomechanics
resources.notes: Undergraduate biomechanics course applying continuum and statistical mechanics from molecular through tissue scales; includes lecture notes, problem sets, and projects.

resources.title: Molecular, Cellular and Tissue Biomechanics (BE.410J)
resources.notes: Graduate biomechanics curriculum covering tissue, cellular and molecular mechanics and experimental methods; includes lecture notes, problem sets, written assignments and exams.

resources.title: Noninvasive Imaging in Biology and Medicine
resources.notes: Theory and application of X-ray CT, PET/SPECT, MRI and optical imaging with emphasis on neuroimaging; includes problem sets and hands-on imaging-system demonstrations.

resources.title: Biomaterials-Tissue Interactions
resources.notes: Graduate instruction in materials science, mechanics and cell biology for implantable and injectable biomedical devices, with lecture videos, notes and readings.

resources.title: Tissue Engineering and Organ Regeneration
resources.notes: Modern graduate curriculum on tissue engineering, organ regeneration, biomaterial scaffolds, cells and regulators, clinical translation, and analysis of regenerative-device successes and failures.

resources.title: Principles and Practice of Tissue Engineering
resources.notes: Graduate tissue-engineering curriculum covering cells, scaffolds, regulators, mechanical loading, culture conditions, fabrication of implantable products and clinical case studies.

resources.title: LL EduCATE: Bioengineering
resources.notes: Introductory high-school/non-credit orientation to bioengineering specializations including prosthetics, medical devices, imaging, artificial organs and biomaterials; useful for foundation exposure, not proof of professional competence.

known_gaps: rehabilitation_engineering still needs a dedicated authoritative instructional source
neural_engineering remains thinner than biomechanics, imaging, biomaterials and tissue engineering and needs a dedicated assessed curriculum
biosensors and bioelectronics need deeper assessed design-and-laboratory coursework
regulatory references support compliance knowledge but do not establish medical-device design competence
research references and graduate courses do not by themselves establish expert readiness
expert readiness requires runtime retrieval, practical design projects, verification and validation, provenance, and passed assessment
